title: US and Ukrainian delegations hold talks in Geneva on the 28-point plan
body:
On Sunday, 23 November 2025, US and Ukrainian delegations met in Geneva, Switzerland, to discuss a US-drafted 28-point blueprint to end the war. Ukraine's envoys were led by presidential chief of staff Andrii Yermak, together with Rustem Umerov of the National Security and Defense Council. The US side included Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll and special envoy Steve Witkoff. European partners were in close contact.

The Associated Press reported that the plan had alarmed Kyiv and European capitals because it accommodated many Russian demands, including territorial concessions that Ukraine had rejected. Senators said Rubio had called it a Russian "wish list," which the State Department denied.

Rubio called the first session "probably the most productive and meaningful meeting" since the Trump administration took office. Yermak reported "very good progress." A second meeting was set for later that day. Rubio said the plan had to be signed off by both presidents and approved by Russia.

Before the talks, President Donald Trump criticised Ukraine for a lack of gratitude for US military aid and did not criticise Russia. He wrote that the invasion "would have NEVER HAPPENED" with strong leadership in both countries. President Volodymyr Zelensky said "a positive result is needed for all of us," that bloodshed must stop, and that the American proposals might reflect "a number of elements" important to Ukraine's national interests.
